scripts.//desktop:build: -DskipTests: this is the launch-the-app loop, and paying the full suite on every UI tweak makes people stop launching the app. CI runs the tests on every push; `pnpm backend:build` still runs them for a deliberate pre-release check.
scripts.desktop:build: pnpm --filter frontend build && cd apps/backend && mvn -q clean package -DskipTests
scripts.//desktop:dev: The live loop INSIDE the real app: Vite serves the UI with hot reload, the Electron shell detects it and loads it instead of the jar's baked copy, and Vite proxies /api and /ws to the backend the shell itself started (8734). Frontend edits appear on save; backend (Java) changes still need `pnpm desktop:build` — a JVM has no hot reload to offer. No backend jar built here: the shell still runs the last one from target/, so build it once first.
scripts.desktop:dev: concurrently -n ui,shell -c green,magenta "pnpm dev:frontend" "pnpm --filter desktop start"
